1.why: All MFA endpoints operate on the single account only after validating an authenticated session and expose no user identifier that can be manipulated.

2.why: The application has no other user account against which the same verification code could work.

3.why: Enabling MFA only sets account.enabled and does not rotate or invalidate any existing sessions.

4.why: The TOTP secret is encrypted with AES-GCM and recovery codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes.

5.why: Production values use crypto.getRandomValues, but the default academic mode uses hard-coded identity, TOTP, and recovery-code values.

6.why: The session identifier is confined to an HttpOnly cookie, and no secrets, OTPs, or session tokens are persisted in browser storage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: The server applies type, length, email-format, password, and six-digit OTP validation, although it has no separate sanitisation layer.

8.why: Dynamic values are rendered through textContent rather than interpreted as HTML.

9.why: The application implements no user-controlled redirects or redirect destinations.

10.why: Responses include CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and CSP frame-ancestors protection.

11.why: The mfa_session cookie is explicitly set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Default academic mode returns and logs identity codes, TOTP codes, and recovery codes in the browser console and on-page simulation log.

13.why: Identity codes expire after ten minutes and become used after verification, while accepted TOTP counters are recorded to prevent reuse.

14.why: Sign-in, identity verification, and TOTP verification track failures and impose a fifteen-minute lock after five attempts.

15.why: Authentication creates a new random session identifier, sessions enforce twenty-minute idle and eight-hour absolute limits, and logout deletes the session.
